title: Payment Confirmation Polling Plan
summary: Plan for tri-state browser polling that reconciles Nuvei confirmation, commercetools Payment state, and DMN webhooks.
notes: Manifest declared DOC, so classification used the manifest override. The document contains planning guidance, outcome contracts, processor/enabler responsibilities, constraints, and testing requirements, but no ADR status or accepted decision marker.
requirements: Processor confirmation/status responses should use PaymentOutcome values approved, rejected, or pending.
Processor should use hard HTTP errors only for invalid requests, including invalid session authentication, wrong cart/payment access, malformed payload, or correlation mismatch.
Enabler should start polling only after browser confirmation returns pending or another retryable inconclusive result.
Enabler should poll only the processor and never Nuvei directly.
Enabler should keep polling requests non-overlapping.
Enabler should stop immediately on approved or rejected outcomes.
Enabler should stop after a bounded timeout and report unresolved timeout as pending/processing rather than a hard error.
Enabler should preserve the original paymentReference and sessionToken during polling.
Pending should be first-class in the enabler public contract, with onPending or an explicit PaymentResult outcome shape.

Tests should cover immediate approved/rejected outcomes, pending-to-final polling outcomes, timeout-to-pending behavior, temporary Nuvei outage handling, DMN-pre-finalized payments, duplicate polls, invalid access, and mismatched sessionToken rejection.
constraints: Nuvei DMN webhooks remain the asynchronous source of truth and final reconciliation fallback.
Processor remains stateless and must not implement in-memory per-payment cadence or rate limiting.
Processor checks commercetools Payment state before calling Nuvei.
Processor calls Nuvei getPaymentStatus only when the Payment is not final.
Processor updates commercetools Payment idempotently when Nuvei returns a final state.
Missing transaction IDs on approved Nuvei responses are unsafe and must not be treated as clean success.
DMN processing must remain idempotent because browser confirmation/status and DMN can race.
Nuvei sessionToken should not be placed in query parameters because URLs are commonly logged.
Nuvei temporary, pending, unknown, or unreachable states should normally become pending rather than hard rejection unless the request itself is invalid.
Long polling cadence should not be encoded on both browser and processor sides; browser/enabler owns cadence and timeout.
